description: Solo participant working on this challenge independently! Not looking for additional team members.
summary: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive web story that teaches 4th-5th grade space fans about NASA hardware left on the Moon, on Mars, and in deep space. Readers meet four machines (Surveyor 3, the Apollo Moon buggy, the Opportunity rover, and Voyager 1). Each tells its own first person story, including why it was sent, what it discovered, and where it is now. The challenge asks for engaging, story driven education about discarded equipment, and this project answers it by turning mission history into easily understandable stories! It matters because young people mostly hear about active missions, and these machines show how past exploration made today’s discoveries possible.
details: The site is a single web page with four chapters, one per machine. Readers pick a machine and read its story, then see three short boxes: why it went, what it found, and where it is now. Stories are written in first person for 4th-5th graders. It works on phones and desktops, supports light and dark mode, uses keyboard friendly buttons, and has text labels on the illustrations. Built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Claude helped write the code, parts of the story text, and illustrations; illustrations are labeled as AI-generated. Facts were checked against NASA mission pages. No NASA logos or branding are used. The intended impact is to spark curiosity in young readers about the history of space exploration!
